title: Australia news live: most banks now predict another rate hike; Ken Henry delivers warning over ‘stupid’ GST deal
text: 21.14 EDT Banks tip another rate rise after inflation figures Unexpectedly strong inflation figures have forced a rethink on interest rates, with three out of four big banks now tipping the RBA to hike rates again by Melbourne Cup day. AAP reports economists at NAB and Commonwealth Bank followed ANZ in changing their rates forecast on Thursday. ANZ was the first of Australia’s biggest lenders to switch their call from an extended hold to one more rise on Wednesday, after July consumer price figures showed underlying inflation rose 0.5% in the month, well above expectations. While ANZ and CBA predict the Reserve Bank will lift the cash rate in November, NAB experts think it will be even sooner, forecasting a hike at the central bank’s next meeting in September. Even though headline inflation slowed on an annual basis from 3.8 to 3.5%, the broad-based rise in underlying inflation suggests the RBA’s preferred quarterly trimmed mean measure will probably come in above 1% in September, NAB said. Read more here: Fears grow for fourth rate hike after Australia sees higher-than-expected July inflation Read more

title: Anthony Albanese says 34 Australians among hundreds of people missing in deadly Nepal flash floods
text: Mudslide submerges China-Nepal crossing point – video Australia news Anthony Albanese says 34 Australians among hundreds of people missing in deadly Nepal flash floods Powerful floods in Himalayan border area sweep away houses, roads and bridges Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kat Wong , Henry Belot and Guardian staff Wed 26 Aug 2026 22.43 EDT First published on Wed 26 Aug 2026 17.16 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Dozens of Australian tourists are reportedly missing in the deadly flash floods that swept through the Nepal-Tibet border, as the Australian government says it is urgently working to confirm their welfare. The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said on Thursday morning there were 34 Australians missing. According to the Nepal Tourist Board, as reported by Press Association, at least 403 people have been reported missing, with 341 foreign nationals unaccounted for. According to the tourist board, 203 of the missing are male and 200 female. title: Nepal flash flood live updates: search on for hundreds missing near Tibet border as officials warn death toll could rise higher
text: 20.55 EDT Summary: at least 160 killed in Nepal flash flood as search for hundreds missing continues Authorities in Nepal and Tibet have said they fear the death toll from catastrophic flooding could be much higher than 160 people already killed, as search and rescue efforts to locate the hundreds missing continue. A huge wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, triggering the flash flood that washed away houses, roads and border crossings. Verified videos showed dozens of people swept away at the border, with authorities on both sides ⁠fearing far higher casualties and massive destruction. Officials in Tibet said they feared “major casualties” after a mudslide hit a border land crossing in the county of Gyirong. As darkness fell, authorities continued the grim task of recovering ‌and trying to identify bodies. Nepal police said 157 bodies had been recovered ‌so far. Three people were reported killed on the Tibet side of the border. title: Democratic states sue to block postal service from carrying out Trump’s mail-in voting order – as it happened
text: 11.31 EDT Democratic states sue to block postal service from carrying out Trump's mail-in voting order Two dozen states and the District of Columbia filed a fresh lawsuit on Wednesday to block Donald Trump’s executive order restricting mail voting in this year’s midterm elections. The challenge comes days after the supreme court’s conservative majority lifted one injunction from a federal judge blocking parts of the president’s order. In their new filing against the US Postal Service (USPS), the states point to concrete steps the administration has taken to carry out Trump’s directive – including a final USPS rule on ballot delivery posted Friday night. The states said that the USPS policy is part of “a broader effort” by the Trump administration “to rewrite federal election law and usurp the authority of the states and Congress”. And a reminder, that the constitution confers control over elections to states and Congress, not the executive. On Monday, the supreme court did not rule on the legality of Trump’s order, but said that the states’ litigation was premature, effectively making room for further legal challenges. text: Пекин готовится ослепить ВВС США одним ударом По данным Блумберг, Китай разработал гиперзвуковой планирующий боевой блок (ГПББ), способный доставлять ракеты класса «воздух–воздух» к цели на расстоянии в тысячи километров . Если система будет доведена до ума, под угрозой окажутся не только американские истребители, а самая ценная авиация — самолеты ДРЛОиУ E-3/E-7 , воздушные командные пункты Е-6B/Е-4B и самолеты-заправщики KC-46 и KC-135 , без которых невозможно проведение масштабных воздушных операций. Сегодня максимальная дальность поражения воздушных целей китайской связкой Цзянь-16 + ракета PL-17 оценивается в 1400 км . Новый проект должен значительно расширить этот рубеж. В качестве носителя рассматриваются ракеты Дунфэн-17 с ГПББ, а в перспективе — более дальнобойная Дунфэн-27. При этом речь идет не о прямом поражении цели баллистической ракетой, а о доставке в заданный район специальной ракеты «воздух–воздух», которая уже на конечном участке должна перехватить самолет. Однако сама ракета — лишь часть системы. Чтобы поразить воздушную цель на такой дистанции, необходимо непрерывно сопровождать ее полет. Для этого Китай активно строит единую сеть разведки и целеуказания, объеди
